title: MemoryStream
description: Work with in-memory byte streams for efficient I/O without temporary files.

data.text: `MemoryStream` is a stream backed by a byte array in memory. It is part of `System.IO` and is useful for processing data without touching the filesystem.
`MemoryStream` is included in the base class library. No extra package is needed.
Write bytes to a `MemoryStream`, then read them back or convert to an array.

data.title: Read and Write with MemoryStream

data.text: `MemoryStream` implements `Stream`, so you can pass it anywhere a stream is expected, such as JSON serialization or HTTP content.

data.title: Serialize to MemoryStream

terms.definition: A stream backed by an in-memory byte array.
The current read/write cursor in the stream.
Copies the stream contents to a new byte array.

data.title: Tip
data.text: Reuse MemoryStream instances with `SetLength(0)` to reduce allocations.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: MemoryStream is ideal for in-memory byte manipulation.
It implements Stream, so it is interchangeable with file streams.
Reset Position before reading after writing.
data.takeaway: MemoryStream eliminates temporary files and reduces disk I/O.
